findings.title: canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all groups
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This looks copied from `canView()`. The effect is that an admin with only a read-only "view all groups" permission passes `requireManage()`.

`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` uses `requireManage()`, so such an admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to the top level. This is a privilege escalation.

The interface Javadoc for `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same wrong behavior and should also be fixed. Only `MANAGE` should be checked.

No test covers this: `testManageAllGroups` only grants MANAGE. There is no test that VIEW alone does not allow creating groups.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and looks up resources by the wrong key
findings.body:
The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to `hasPermission`. That method calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so a resource ID is used as a name and never matches. Evaluation always falls back to the all-groups resource.

The callback then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result. Callers treat the result as group IDs: `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` put it in the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute, and `getUsersCount(realm, groupIds)` uses it.

In addition, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never calls `setType`, so `findByType(server, "Groups")` only returns the all-groups resource named "Groups". Per-group resources are never iterated.

Consequences:
- With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission, the set contains the "Groups" resource UUID. The user query is restricted to a non-existent group and returns no users.
- With only per-group permissions, the set is empty. The DB query is unfiltered and users are filtered in memory after pagination, so pages come back short or incomplete.
- `/users/count` returns wrong counts in both cases.

The method should iterate per-group resources and return `resource.getName()` (the group id). The all-groups case needs its own handling.

findings.title: NPE when the all-groups "Groups" resource does not exist
findings.body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` can return null. This happens when the schema is not supported for the current context, or when the "Groups" resource was never created. The result is passed straight into `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()` with no null check.

`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change therefore have no "Groups" resource and none of the new `manage-members`/`view-members`/`manage-membership` scopes.

For such realms, any admin without the `view-users`/`manage-users` roles who lists or reads groups goes through `canView(group)` and hits this path, which fails with a 500. Creating group permissions there also fails with "No scopes found".

Add a null guard here, and either add a migration or create the missing schema resources and scopes for existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: Any per-group permission hides all-groups grants for other scopes on that group
findings.body:
`hasPermission` falls back to the all-groups resource only when no per-group resource exists. Once any permission references a group (for example VIEW_MEMBERS on `topGroup`), that group's resource exists and only it is evaluated.

Per-group resources are created without a type, so the "Groups"-typed all-groups permissions are not included in that evaluation. As a result, an admin with "manage all groups" who is also given "view-members on topGroup" can no longer manage, view, or map roles on `topGroup`.

This also makes `canView()`/`canManage()` (all-groups) and `canView(group)`/`canManage(group)` disagree for the same group. The evaluation should combine the per-group result with the all-groups resource for scopes the per-group permissions do not decide.

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body:
The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementations actually check `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, which is a different scope (MANAGE_MEMBERS vs MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP). It looks copy-pasted from `requireManageMembership` and will mislead callers.

Separately, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` documents its return as a "Stream" while it returns a Set.

findings.title: Public evaluator interface methods renamed/removed without deprecation
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission()` is renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, and `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` is removed. `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes` is also removed.

`GroupPermissionEvaluator` is reachable from `AdminPermissionEvaluator`, which custom admin REST extensions (`AdminRealmResourceProvider`) receive. Those extensions will fail to compile or link after upgrade.

Consider keeping the old method as a deprecated default that delegates to the new one.

findings.title: Groups resource type not handled in getResourceName
findings.body:
The new GROUPS resource type is added, but `getResourceName` still only maps USERS resources to human-readable names ("All users" or the username).

Per-group resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` with the group id as name and no display name. The "Groups" type resource also has no display name. For group permissions this method therefore returns `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null.

Resource names shown for group permissions in the admin API/UI will be null or meaningless instead of "All groups" or the group name/path.

findings.title: testManageGroupMembership does not verify that the group-level permission is required
findings.body:
The test grants all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and per-group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP together, then only asserts that the join succeeds.

The initial negative check uses the non-existent group "no-such", so it only exercises the user-level check. Nothing asserts that the join to `topGroup` is forbidden when the group's MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission is absent, so a regression in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManageMembership` would go unnoticed.

The suite also has no case for all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on user listing or count, which would expose the `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` bug.
